title: Replicate a candidate-masked test of Tucker and Talbert's herbal identifications
statement: Pilot with one annotator. I seeded a sample of six public herbal scans from folio strings in Tucker and Talbert's 2013 article (seed 1503), recorded characters before revealing their proposed taxa, then checked each folio mention in context. The scan numbers remained visible. The f9r string referred to the Cruz-Badianus comparator and was excluded after the reveal. None of the five actual target identifications was recovered to genus from the first pass. At f24r (Yale canvas 1006120), I recorded pale ray-like heads with a central disc and green backing. The paper proposes Silene, possibly S. menziesii, and itself notes discordant leaf bases. At f6v (1006087), I recorded deeply lobed leaves and round spiny bodies and volunteered castor as a possibility. The paper proposes two Cnidoscolus taxa. The Flora of China entry for Ricinus communis independently documents both palmately lobed leaves and spiny capsules (https://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200012604), so these two broad features leave a competing genus open. At f32r (1006136), I recorded broad mostly paired leaves and terminal clusters of unresolved blue and pale bodies before revealing Ocimum campechianum. At f5v (1006085), I recorded red star-like structures, jagged palmate foliage and a thickened base, consistent with broad traits the authors cite for Jatropha cathartica. At f25r (1006122), I recorded broad nearly paired leaves and red material at nodes, with no clear flowers, before revealing Urtica chamaedryoides. Canvas base is https://collections.library.yale.edu/manifests/oid/2002046/canvas/ and the open source article is https://web.archive.org/web/20150226041323/http://cms.herbalgram.org/herbalgram/issue100/HG100-voynich-online.pdf. These results measure this annotator's recovery on a small sample. Independent confirmation and the animal and mineral claims remain open. Hodgins's University of Arizona report dates parchment samples (https://www.voynich.nu/papers/Carbon_GH_2009.pdf). A visual identification cannot establish the date of the ink or explain the proposed gap between parchment preparation and use.
check: Extract a verified list of Beinecke folio and taxon pairs from the article before sampling. Mask proposed names, folio labels and provenance, use at least two independent annotators, and record leaf, fruit or flower and root characters before reveal. Then compare each proposed taxon against equally plausible alternatives including non-American taxa, with a none-of-these option. Report agreement at family, genus and species levels. Use confirmed illustration candidates for anchors only when a specific nearby Voynich label can be tied to the image.
